notes:
Summary: Large European payments processor evaluating Redwood for embeddings + enrichment + support assistant. Primary requirement = strict EU-only data residency (no cross-border replication, no US control plane). Worked closely with SE (Luca) on performance and quantization recommendations for cost control. Legal insists on physical tenancy in EU region and auditable control plane; Redwood's current Private offering requires customer-managed control plane but cannot commit to operator-free EU-only tenancy SLA requested by EuroGuard. Procurement weighed pricing and features but chose local EU vendor (DataSentry) citing contractual residency guarantees and prior FedRAMP-like statement for EU operations.

Key quotes and shorthand from calls: "Can’t accept any tokenization or telemetry leaving EU — this is non-negotiable." — Head of Legal.
"We liked the latency and cost math, but residency is deal-breaker." — CTO.

Current posture: Closed/stalled — buyer moved to local provider. No solid internal champion after CTO left for competitor in Q4. Recommended follow-ups: file competitive loss review, surface residency roadmap to product + legal, keep 6mo cadence for re-engagement if Redwood introduces EU-only tenancy or certified EU control plane.
outcome_summary: Stalled -> closed-lost to local EU provider due to inability to provide EU-only tenancy/residency guarantee. Budget freeze and no internal champion accelerated loss. Technical fit was good but residency and contractual controls were decisive.
